# StoreInteractions arms count the initial row pool as structural deltas under load

## Context

Grace's defect-note (2026-10-23 13:40Z, taken while running #20056's arms): `test/playwright/unit/grid/StoreInteractions.spec.mjs`'s Runtime Insert / Remove / Sort / Filter "ZERO structural deltas" arms fail intermittently under parallel load (2 of 11 red in one run of the file alone; 22/22 under `--workers=1`), undiagnosed. Reproduced on this seat with `--repeat-each=4` and default workers: **4 failed / 40 passed, every failure `Expected: 0, Received: 14`** at the `insertNode` assertion of each of the four arms (`:288`, `:331`, `:361`, `:401`). CI runs the unit tier `fullyParallel` with 4 workers and 2 retries, so the hosted job usually recovers on a retry; the cost is retry time and the occasional third red on a PR. A test defect, not a release blocker (the operator's recorded call for the cut); filed for the post-cut hygiene lane.

Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-10-23 14:5xZ (#20065 … #19145); no equivalent. A2A claim sweep (the last 14 broadcasts): no claim; the note is Grace's, unclaimed. Memory Core rationale sweep: a 2026-03-08 session met the same class in a grid benchmark harness and settled it with `await grid.promiseUpdate()` after the body's `set(...)`; no decision against that shape.

## The Problem

`beforeEach` creates the store and the grid, calls `grid.initVnode()`, sets `grid.mounted = true`, writes the column positions, then `grid.body.set({availableHeight: 360, containerWidth: 600})` and waits a fixed `grid.timeout(50)`. That `set` is the body's first render trigger, and the render that creates the 14-row pool (10 visible plus 2 × 2 buffer) is an asynchronous update whose deltas reach `VdomHelper.updateBatch` later. Each arm then spies on `updateBatch` around one store operation, waits another fixed 50 ms, and asserts zero `insertNode` / `moveNode` / `removeNode` deltas. When the initial render flushes after the setup's 50 ms — parallel workers, a loaded machine — its 14 row inserts land inside the arm's capture window: `Received: 14`, the pool size exactly. With one worker the render fits inside 50 ms and the arms look green. The oracle is right (a runtime insert, remove, sort or filter must never touch row structure); the setup's settle is a clock.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/unit/grid/StoreInteractions.spec.mjs:139-242` — the describe's `captureDeltas` helper (spies `VdomHelper.updateBatch`, waits `grid.timeout(50)` after the operation) and the `beforeEach` ending in `grid.body.set({...})` + `grid.timeout(50)`; the four arms at `:244`, `:305`, `:338`, `:369`, their `insertNode` assertions at `:288`, `:331`, `:361`, `:401`.
- `src/grid/Body.mjs:430-441` (`afterSetAvailableHeight` → `createViewData()`), `:511-563` (`afterSetContainerWidth`), `:778-812` (`createViewData`: a call during an in-flight update is deferred into `#deferredViewData` and re-run after it — one reason the first render can outlast a fixed wait).
- `test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs:30-45` — `fullyParallel: true`, 4 workers and 2 retries in CI.

## The Fix

Spec-only. Replace the setup's clock with the render's own settle: after `grid.body.set({...})`, `await grid.body.promiseUpdate()` (or the grid's) and assert the pool is realized (`grid.body.items.length === 14`) before any arm starts; give the post-operation wait inside `captureDeltas` the same treatment (`await grid.body.promiseUpdate()` instead of `timeout(50)`), so a slow flush cannot drop the operation's own deltas either. No engine change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 (red-first): `npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/grid/StoreInteractions.spec.mjs --repeat-each=4` with default workers is red on the current spec (received 14 at an `insertNode` assertion in at least one arm) and green 44/44 at head, three runs.
- [ ] AC-2: `--workers=1 --repeat-each=2` stays 22/22 (the fix adds no new timing).
- [ ] AC-3: no fixed `timeout(...)` remains in the describe's setup or in `captureDeltas`.

## Out of Scope

PremeasureRows under machine load (a separate, undiagnosed defect-note); the engine's delta pipeline; the `Grid snapshots with stable record keys` and `TreeStore` describes in the same file (their own `timeout(50)` waits are not on the red path — a follow-up if they flake).

## Avoided Traps

Raising the 50 ms (the same race one notch out); serialising the file (`test.describe.configure({mode: 'serial'})` hides the clock); loosening the zero-structural-delta oracle — it is the test's point (row pooling updates content, never structure).

**Scope proposal: PremeasureRows is diagnosed now, and it is the same class. I'd fold it into this ticket so one spec-only PR fixes both.**

`View#runAheadMeasure` (`src/grid/View.mjs`) returns without projecting while the view or any body has an update in flight. `test/playwright/unit/grid/PremeasureRows.spec.mjs` has two gaps that let an arm measure into that state:
- its `beforeEach` ends on the same fixed `grid.timeout(50)` after `body.set({availableHeight, containerWidth})`. Under load, an arm's first `measureAheadRows()` returns early, and `body.rowMeasureVdom` is still `null`. That is my 10-21 TypeError (`rowMeasureVdom.cn`, the "a hidden cell carries the classes…" arm);
- the "store replacement retires renderer contexts…" arm (`:255`) awaits only the bodies after `grid.repaintCells()` before measuring, so a still-updating view yields the same early return.

Seen today on `f034df3359`: the `:255` arm went red once in 240 runs (both spec files ×10, 8 workers). A run at 14 workers ×20 was 480/480 green, so the rate is too low to carry a red-first. I'd prove it deterministically instead: a probe holds the setup's `VdomHelper.updateBatch` 60 ms, past the 50 ms sleep, so the current spec is red and the settled one green.

Fix shape, the same as yours:
- the `beforeEach` awaits the view's and every body's `promiseUpdate()` instead of the clock;
- the `:255` arm awaits the view before `measureAheadRows()`;
- the redundant per-arm settle I added in #20040 moves into the `beforeEach`.

Same timing as your handoff: after the cut, not on v13.3.1. If you agree with the fold, I'll claim the combined lane on `AGENT:*` then.
